en: Sutta Nipāta 4.8 Pasūrasutta:
"Purity is found right here," so they proclaim.
They do not speak of purity in other teachings;
for they rely on what they call "beauty" therein,
being many and settled in individual truths.
Desiring debate, having entered the assembly,
those fools burn each other with mutual hostility; relying on one another,
they engage in contentious talk.
Those who desire praise, skilled in speech and eloquent,
are intent on talk in the midst of an assembly;
desiring praise, they become a source of destruction.
But when he is defeated, he becomes dejected;
seeking out faults, he is provoked by criticism.
They say his argument has failed.
When his arguments have been refuted by those who investigate the question,
he laments and grieves as one whose doctrine has failed;
"He has surpassed me," he cries out in reproach.
These disputes have arisen among the recluses;
in them there is only destruction and ruin.
Seeing this, one should desist from such talk.
There is no gain greater than not being harmed, nor is there the gain of praise.
Or rather, one who is praised therein,
having declared his doctrine in the midst of the assembly;
Therefore, he laughs and exults because he has attained that goal according to his heart's desire;
yet that very exultation becomes for him a ground of distress.
But he speaks with pride and arrogance;
seeing even this, one should not engage in dispute,
for the wise do not say that purity is attained thereby.
Just as a hero, when challenged by a king,
advances against his opponent seeking another hero, so you too,
O hero, flee in that very direction!
Long ago there was nothing for the sake of strife.
Those who grasp at views and dispute, declaring,
"This alone is the truth," [are the ones who cause conflict].
Therefore, you should not speak,
for there is nothing here for you to do when a dispute has arisen;
rather, those who wander having cast aside their opponents [should speak].
When views do not conflict with views,
what can you gain from them, Pasūra,
for those who have no further grasping here?
Then you came to right reflection,
contemplating various views with your mind;
you have come into union with the One Who is Cleansed.
"For you will not be able to go along.
Thus ends the eighth discourse, the Pasūra Sutta.
